- When sentiment is strongly positive (≥ 0.67) in recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast peaks by 10–20%.
- When sentiment is strongly negative (≤ -0.67), model underestimates; increase forecast lows by 10–20%.
- Model consistently overreacts to short-term spikes in sentiment; apply a 1–2 day lag correction to avoid overshoot.
- Mean reversion is strong in 30-day horizon; if forecast is >2σ above recent 18-day mean, reduce by 15–30%.
- In high-sentiment periods, model often fails to capture sustained upward momentum; adjust forecast slope downward by 5–15% for 5–7 day horizons.
- If sentiment history shows alternating highs/lows, model tends to misalign with trend direction; align forecast with sentiment polarity shift, not absolute value.
